runs.name: RPM International Inc.
runs.entry: Price **$97.73** (close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged) x **127,533,690 shares** (10-Q cover, 0001193125-26-415321; one class; issued 146,910 thousand less treasury 19,356 thousand agrees within the quarter's buyback) = cap **$12,464M**; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y par, 2026-10-09). Q1 IN (specialty coatings, sealants, roofing and DIY products sold mostly for repair and maintenance; $7.86B of sales; three segments from FY2026) · Q2 IN (CPG decides: about 10% pre-tax on sales FY2008 to FY2020, no loss through 2009, 14% to 15% since FY2021, the recent gain not credited without a downturn; ten-year pre-tax return on sales 10.4% against Sherwin-Williams 14.0%, PPG 11.4%, Axalta 9.9%, H.B. Fuller 8.8%, Carlisle 15.2%; Sika, Holcim, Saint-Gobain, Henkel and Soprema named, not SEC filers) · Q3 for, modestly (high return on tangible capital) · Q4 weighs against, no STOP (adjusted EBITDA featured; restructuring every year; owner cash FY2022 -$83.8M on an inventory build, FY2024 $882.4M on the release) · **Q5 OUT on integrity, on doubt: the SEC's case on the FY2013 DOJ overcharge investigation (Litigation Release 23639: the General Counsel and Chief Compliance Officer kept the rising overcharge estimates, at least $28M, from the CEO, CFO, audit committee and auditors; three FY2013 quarters restated; the company called the case "without merit", 10-K FY2017); settled 2020 with a $2.0M penalty and injunctions, neither admitted nor denied, the General Counsel enjoined under the books-and-records rule (Litigation Release 24994); the board kept him as compliance officer and a named executive into fiscal 2025, four current directors including the Lead Director serving through it; the headline measure moved to adjusted EBITDA. For: the CEO and CFO never charged; the FY2024 to FY2026 long-term awards paid 0%.** Q6 to Q12 not reached. After the stop, COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash five-year mean $449.3M all spending ($547.3M on maintenance spending; acquisitions net $164.7M a year), literal window FY2022 to FY2026 kept as the base since it holds both the build and the release; shown growth 12.5% capped at the 5.9% sales growth (a CONVENTION of the run, the uncapped case beside); range $71.94 to $89.52 all-equity ($76.63 to $87.22 equity-only) against $97.73, returns 4.3% to 5.3% at the price (8.1% uncapped), no case earns the floor; fair $34.36 all-equity, $42.57 equity-only. No fair-price alert is armed: the box is not OUT at Q7 (the cycle prompt's rule). Run by an interactive batch session, killed after Q4 (1b701c47); resumed by the overnight cycle's dispatched analyst (Q5 f6804362, close 57ee556b), which corrected three errors in its own uncommitted Q5 draft before committing (board twelve nominees, eleven independent; the General Counsel a named executive into fiscal 2025; the FY2026 cash bonus at 120% of target). The dispatcher re-checked: check_framework PASS; the analyst's check_quotes.py 69 ids, no E-ids, none missing; the dispatcher's dispatcher_quote_check.py 35 fragments, 0 problems; no tracked research file over 200 KB. The analyst's own doubt, stated: a reader weighing the age of the matter and the new board more heavily could pass Q5; the box would stay OUT on the Q7 arithmetic. Framework points for the operator (from the run): how growth Q2 declined to credit is removed from Q7's growth; no fallback for (a) and (b) where the cash series changes sign; whether the no-growth end buys nothing in years one to ten; Q5's doubt rule leans on the short row [M2013-088]; no box wording for a file closed at Q5 itself. Strongest other evidence against: Consumer organic sales down four of five years, a few retailers about two-thirds of the segment; a $110.8M judgment plus interest accrued at $0.5M; buybacks at $104 to $120. Could not get: about $100M of the FY2026 rise in prepaid and other assets unexplained. Position note filled at the fold: not held. The v4.1 bands retired.
runs.narr: A maker of specialty coatings, sealants and roofing sold mainly for repair, whose construction segment has held about 10% pre-tax through a full cycle; stopped at Q5 on doubt over the SEC's FY2013 case, in which the General Counsel kept the overcharge estimates from the board and auditors and the board kept him as compliance officer for years after the injunction. The arithmetic after the stop sits below the price on every case.
